The target of DNA polymerase iota is a complex molecule, [(3S,8S,9R,10R,12R,13S,14R,17S)-17-acetyl-3,8,14,17-tetrahydroxy-10,13-dimethyl-1,2,3,4,7,9,11,12,15,16-decahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-12-yl] pyridine-3-carboxylate, which is directly targeted by Ethyl isostearate. The relationship between Ethyl isostearate and SF-539 is further supported by the direct targeting of the latter by the complex molecule, implying that Ethyl isostearate may influence SF-539 through this pathway. The evidence suggests a possible mechanism where Ethyl isostearate modulates DNA polymerase iota, which in turn affects the activity of [(3S,8S,9R,10R,12R,13S,14R,17S)-17-acetyl-3,8,14,17-tetrahydroxy-10,13-dimethyl-1,2,3,4,7,9,11,12,15,16-decahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-12-yl] pyridine-3-carboxylate, ultimately influencing SF-539.
